snippet.title: Millionenstreit um Torf: Wurde illegal abgebaut? | Doku | NDR Story
snippet.description:
In Niedersachsens Mooren fehlen offenbar Tonnen an Torf. Der Verdacht: Er wurde illegal abgebaut. Wie groß ist der Schaden für die Natur?

Torfabbau in Niedersachsen steht unter Verdacht: Auf Flächen auch in Naturschutzgebieten soll deutlich tiefer abgebaut worden sein als erlaubt. Das Problem: Die Flächen sollen nach dem Torfabbau wiedervernässt werden, es sollen also wieder intakte, nasse Moore entstehen und dafür braucht es laut Fachleuten eine ausreichend dicke Torfschicht, die nach dem Abbau stehenbleibt. Doch NDR Recherchen zeigen: Auf vielen Fächen ist das offenbar nicht der Fall. Es geht um mögliche Millionenschäden und Behörden, die teils jahrelang kaum eingriffen. Manche Unternehmer räumen nun Verstöße ein, andere schweigen oder weisen Vorwürfe von sich. Wie groß ist der Schaden – und wer trägt die Verantwortung?

Mehr zu der Recherche: https://www.ndr.de/nachrichten/info/moore-in-niedersachsen-wurde-ueber-jahre-zu-viel-torf-abgebaut,torf-110.html
Homepage NDR Story: www.ndr.de/ndrstory

snippet.title: Does Andrea Piardi Even Understand Rugby's Laws? | France vs SA (Part 2)
snippet.description:
Does Andrea Piardi actually understand the laws he's supposed to enforce? Because after watching his performance during France's 21–19 victory over South Africa, I genuinely have my doubts.

In Part 2 of my France vs South Africa refereeing analysis, we examine one of the most frustrating aspects of Piardi's officiating: his failure to penalise France for repeated knee-drop tackles on Springbok ball carriers.

Throughout the match, French defenders repeatedly appeared to drop onto their knees while tackling, attempting to bring powerful South African ball carriers to ground. Yet despite the infringements and the growing frustration of the Springbok players, Piardi continued to allow these tackles.

His explanation? The actions happened "simultaneously."

But here's where things get particularly embarrassing.

World Rugby literally has an official instructional video on its own website demonstrating these exact types of illegal tackles.

In this analysis, we compare the French tackles directly against World Rugby's own explanations and video examples.

The similarities raise some serious questions.

How can the governing body produce instructional material explaining these infringements, yet its appointed referee seemingly fails to recognise them during one of the biggest international matches of the year?

Was Piardi misunderstanding the law? Was he applying a different interpretation? Or was this simply another example of inconsistent refereeing?

And perhaps the biggest question of all:

How does World Rugby continue to justify appointing referees to major international fixtures when performances like this raise such serious concerns?

The Springboks weren't perfect, and France deserve credit for their victory. But that doesn't mean the standard of officiating should escape scrutiny.

Players are expected to know the laws. Coaches are expected to understand them. Supporters are expected to accept them.

Surely it's reasonable to expect the referee to apply them consistently?

This video isn't about blindly defending South Africa. It's about examining the footage, comparing the decisions against World Rugby's own guidance, and demanding accountability at the highest level of rugby.

Dear World Rugby, we're not blind.

snippet.description:
ÚLTIMA HORA | Países Bajos prepara supermercados de emergencia ante una guerra o un apagón masivo

Los supermercados de Países Bajos se preparan para afrontar un escenario de emergencia extrema que podría dejar a la población sin acceso al suministro habitual de alimentos durante un periodo prolongado. Según informa el diario neerlandés AD, la Asociación Comercial Central (CBL) trabaja en un plan nacional para transformar establecimientos estratégicos en tiendas de emergencia capaces de seguir operando ante una guerra, un ciberataque a gran escala o un apagón generalizado.   

El proyecto busca garantizar que todos los ciudadanos neerlandeses puedan llegar en coche a un supermercado de emergencia en un máximo de 15 minutos para acceder a productos básicos aunque fallen las infraestructuras y cadenas de suministro ordinarias, sumándose a las medidas de preparación civil impulsadas en países como Reino Unido, Japón o Australia.
